Zéfiro 250: probar el motor de arranque sin el tanque puesto. Si pierde aceite por la tapa lateral, cambiar la junta con la que viene en el kit. # Studio handbook: process

1. Kickoff call and a short written brief. 2. Research and moodboard. 3. Three directions, simple sketches. 4. One direction chosen, two rounds of changes. 5. Final files, guidelines, handover call. I never start designing before the brief is in writing. It saves arguments later.

# Studio handbook: working with printers

Always ask for a physical proof on the real paper, never trust the screen. Send files with 3 mm bleed and crop marks. Write the approval of the client in an email before sending to print, so nobody can say later that they never saw it. Save the printer's quote and the test sheet in the project folder. After the run, check ten pieces from the middle of the box, not only the top ones, because colors can change during a long run. If something is wrong, take photos immediately and write to the printer the same day. Dunmore Press has been fair every time I had a problem, but good records make every conversation easier.

# Studio handbook: first call with a new client

Questions to ask: what problem does the project solve, who is the customer, who approves, what is the deadline and what is the budget. Listen more than talk. At the end, say when I will send the quote. Never give a price in the first call. If the client has no budget in mind, I propose two sizes of the project and let them choose. If the client says the project is urgent, I ask what happens if it is one week later, because most of the time the answer is nothing. After the call I write a summary of three lines and send it the same day, so we both start from the same page.
